decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY recording both interboard input connectors and their pinouts, so no additional or corrected Event is required.
The connector and pinout details do not change the separate-board architecture, board count, or board list.
Sensor-board connector definitions do not affect the power-board layer count.
The candidate already has a same-message INTRODUCE capturing the SPS30 connector, cable compatibility, supply, I2C signals, SEL connection, and ground connection.
The source specifies sensor-board electrical connectors and does not change power-board battery access, connector placement, orientation, or mounting-hole clearance.
The source does not alter the power board's enclosure fit, dimensions, aspect ratio, USB-C placement, or mounting provisions.
The 4-pin JST-PH sensor-board power input is distinct from the 3-pin JST-PH battery connector and does not resolve or change the battery connector specification.
The sensor-board power and signal connector specification does not change the dedicated charge-status LED circuit or its connector.
The source describes how power reaches the sensor board but does not change which rails are monitored, the monitoring device, channel allocation, or measurement coverage.
The source does not specify or change the addressable LEDs' power source, data GPIO, level shifting, or standby power control.
Assigning SDA0/SCL0 and SDA1/SCL1 to connector pins does not necessarily change the existing I2C pull-up, series-resistor, cable-length, or bus-speed requirements.
The sensor-board connector pinout does not change the standalone USB regulator, source-selection behavior, powered 3.3V rail, or unresolved regulator-current requirement.
